case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.case_name: Department of Health & Rehabilitative Services v. M.B.
key_cases.holding: A child's out-of-court statements that satisfy section 90.803(23)'s reliability safeguards are admissible as substantive evidence in a dependency hearing even when they are inconsistent with the child's in-court testimony, and dependency itself is proved by a preponderance of the evidence.
key_cases.relevance: School, medical and other third-party disclosures typically reach court as child hearsay, and M.B. sets the reliability gate those statements must clear.
key_cases.quote: are admissible as substantive evidence in a dependency hearing once they have satisfied the stringent reliability safeguards established in section 90.803(23) and refined in our prior case law

key_cases.court: District Court of Appeal of Florida, First District
key_cases.holding: A physician who reported suspected child abuse was immune from civil liability under section 39.203 because the record showed no evidence overcoming the good-faith presumption, and summary judgment for the reporter was affirmed.
key_cases.relevance: The good-faith standard applied here is the same one that protects teachers and school staff who report.
key_cases.quote: Section 39.203, Florida Statutes affords a general grant of immunity to a person who makes a report of child abuse in good faith.

key_cases.court: United States Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit
key_cases.holding: Social workers who interviewed a child at school without her father's consent and threatened removal during an investigation the father had invited did not violate clearly established rights, and dismissal of his section 1983 complaint was affirmed.
key_cases.relevance: Loftus is the Eleventh Circuit authority on interviewing a child at school without parental notice or consent.
key_cases.quote: Because neither social worker violated any clearly established federal civil rights in the investigation that Loftus had invited, we affirm the dismissal of Loftus's complaint against them.

mandatory_reporters: Any person (universal mandatory reporting) — Fla. Stat. § 39.201(1)(a)
Physicians, osteopathic physicians, medical examiners, chiropractic physicians, nurses, and hospital personnel — must give their name when reporting, Fla. Stat. § 39.201(1)(b)2.a.
Health care professionals and mental health professionals — must give their name when reporting, Fla. Stat. § 39.201(1)(b)2.b.
Practitioners who rely solely on spiritual means for healing — must give their name when reporting, Fla. Stat. § 39.201(1)(b)2.c.
School teachers and other school officials or personnel — must give their name when reporting, Fla. Stat. § 39.201(1)(b)2.d.
Social workers, day care center workers, and other professional child care, foster care, residential, or institutional workers — must give their name when reporting, Fla. Stat. § 39.201(1)(b)2.e.
Law enforcement officers — must give their name when reporting, Fla. Stat. § 39.201(1)(b)2.f.
Judges — must give their name when reporting, Fla. Stat. § 39.201(1)(b)2.g.
Animal control officers — must give their name when reporting, Fla. Stat. § 39.201(1)(b)2.h.
reporting_details: In Florida any person who knows, or has reasonable cause to suspect, that a child is abused, abandoned, or neglected must report it immediately to the statewide central abuse hotline (Fla. Stat. § 39.201(1)(a)); members of the general public may report anonymously, but reporters in the professions listed in Fla. Stat. § 39.201(1)(b)2. must give their names.

timeline_requirements.deadline: Immediate response, or 24-hour response; an immediate response may be downgraded to a 24-hour response only on information obtained after the Florida Abuse Hotline screening showing that the child is no longer in imminent danger of being harmed

timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Not specified in Fla. Admin. Code R. 65C-29.003
